units.translation: a mirror of companionship, a phantom of a shadow
bronze is a mirror of the form, wine of the mind
since you have accomplished it in your mind
where Turnebus has γαίας [of the earth]. In M γαίαι [to the earth] (i.e. γαίᾳ [to the earth]).
but the opposite of these, held fast by the earth, to be darkened in darkness (Blomfield reads κάτοχα μαυροῦσθαι [held fast, to be darkened])
ἄνω καὶ κάτω [up and down] topsy-turvy
but I will go down beneath the earth's darkness
for I do not speak of the lower earth
to the places below and down under the earth
greatest herald of those above and below
and having withered you while alive, I will lead you down
Zeus – to strengthen the lesser against the stronger, he does not revere anyone seated above, but below
but all other things he turns upside down and sets
sending up from below late-avenging ruin
before you come to the Caucasus itself
to make a noise, to murmur
a wave of men with slanting crests seethes around the city
a wave – which also seethes around the stern of the city
in the verse of an interpolator, about which see under προσαιθρίζω [to expose to the air].
burning more than what has been said
either having burned or having cut
Thus Porson for μαλθάσσῃ λιταῖς ἐμαῖς. κέαρ [soften with my prayers. heart]. Robortellus had seen that κέαρ [heart] should be added.
the son of Cronus has a heart that cannot be soothed
I was pained in my heart
if someone softens the heart at the right time
beware of this, lest his heart ever be grieved
and I am devoured in my heart by anxiety
Zeus warms the heart with love
nor does he soften his heart | with prayers
but his heart does not sleep for fear
for thus the man-counseling heart of a woman prevails, hoping
or indeed to be lifted up by a woman's heart
a heart whirled in fulfilling eddies
and again my dear heart leaps
and no longer would the heart be untouched (I corrected thus for ἄφυκτον [inescapable])
where κεδνῶν [of good things] is contrary to the meter.
a good helmsman of the ship
let us adopt a good and deep-counseling thought
alas, alas, for the good strength
and a good seer of the army
whether having learned good or not
how then could you, speaking good and true things, succeed?
how shall I mix good things with evils?
a pollution that averts both evils and good things
for the sake of good deeds
I will be careful to remember these good commands of yours
changed by a corrector in Min to κήλθον [I came].
Schol. καὶ τὰ πόρρωθεν καλῶς κείμενα τῶν φίλων, ὅ ἐστι τὰ ἐπὶ ξένης ἀγαθὰ ἐνδιαιτήματα [and the good things of friends that are well placed far away, that is, the good dwellings in a foreign land].
it lies near the narrow sea
O revered earth, – who now lie upon the admiral's body
